rationale.complete: Round 1 done: card, impostor table and dated predictions before data; synthetic validation on six real cycle skeletons (bias, coverage, overshoot power, clock and random-walk identification); replication on 37 non-holdout period units in three regimes; 4 natives (NE14, NE04, NE16, NE32); labelled post hoc two-timescale analysis; estimates rows; confirm.py frozen with a passing dry run (not run). Missing: holdout run, a direct state-space fit, content turnover.
rationale.faithfulness: Reversion to an agent set point is robust (37/37 units, all regimes, agent-level gain invariant across periods r 0.52 vs null p95 0.33), and HH269's overshoot is refuted with a demonstrated mechanism (two-snapshot sampling, reproduced synthetically). The pre-registered first-order model fails (AR(2) > 0 in 25/37; phi+ >> b(1+c)); the replacing two-timescale model is post hoc. Scorecard A2 B1 C1 D1 E1 F2 G1 H1 I1.
rationale.usefulness: Practical facts for scaffold builders and monitors: memory size is per-agent regulated (91% agent variance), robust to forced erasures, and a prompt change moves its set point (+17-31% at NE14) rather than the loop gain; raw memory_stats series show a false overshoot from the two-snapshot write. It does not bear on what memory is worth, so the operator value is modest.

one_line: Memory size reverts to an agent set point on the consolidation clock without overshoot; the loop is a near-deadbeat compression around a slowly drifting target, not a first-order homeostat.

models.note: store size regulated; first-order loop and overshoot refuted
import and removal maps explain little persistence

v2.claim: Agent memory size reverts to an agent-specific set point on the consolidation clock (φ⁺ 0.67 per cycle, 37/37 units) with no overshoot; the loop is two-timescale, not first order; H09's apparent overshoot was a sampling artifact (two rows per consolidation)
v2.scope: 37 units; natives NE14, NE04, NE16, NE32
v2.decision: treat agent memory size as a regulated agent property, not a lever

raters.claim: Post-compression memory size relaxes toward an agent-specific set point on the consolidation clock without overshoot (0<phi+<1 in 37/37 units; forced = voluntary), and H09's negative phi is the append/compress two-snapshot sampling artifact. Excluded: the two-timescale model (post hoc), NE04/NE14 gain predictions, the first-order clause (P5 failed).
